excerpts.text: However, in 1800, Spain had ceded the Louisiana territory back to France as part of Napoleon's secret [Third Treaty of San Ildefonso](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Third_Treaty_of_San_Ildefonso "Third Treaty of San Ildefonso").[[8]](#cite_note-10) The subsequent 1801 [Treaty of Aranjuez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Treaty_of_Aranjuez_(1801) "Treaty of Aranjuez (1801)") established that Spain's cession of Louisiana was a "restoration" of the territory to France, not a retrocession.[[9]](#cite_note-Chambers-11) The territory nominally remained under Spanish control, until a transfer of power to France on November 30, 1803, just three weeks before the formal cession of the territory to the United States on December 20, 1803.[[10]](#cite_note-12)

excerpts.text: In the Treaty of Fontainebleau, signed November 3, 1762, France ceded all the territory of [**colonial Louisiana**](https://64parishes.org/entry/french-colonial-louisiana) west of the Mississippi River, along with New Orleans, to Spain.

Under the terms of the Treaty of Paris, France gave up its territory in Canada and the eastern part of Louisiana to the British while Great Britain received Florida for returning the Cuban port of Havana to Spain.
